newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec trade deficit widened 29.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec trade deficit widened 29.6 pct.

text.p: Commerce Department report of U.S. international trade.

The volume of total crude oil and petroleum product imports rose in December to 289.8 million barrels from 248.1 million in November. The total value rose to $6.49 billion in December from $5.43 billion. These data are available only on a Census basis.
The price of imported crude oil rose to an average $21.65 a barrel in December from $21.44 per barrel in November. The value of December crude oil imports rose to $4.66 billion from $4.11 billion.
For all of 1996, the overall U.S. trade deficit rose 8.7 percent to $114.23 billion, the highest since 1988's $115.5 billion. The deficit in goods widened 8.2 percent to a record $187.62 billion.
The 1996 U.S.-Japan trade deficit fell 19.4 percent to $47.68 billion, the lowest since 1991, the department said.

But the deficit with Western Europe rose 51.8 percent to $15.87 billion, the highest since 1987. The U.S.-Canada deficit rose 26 percent to $22.84 billion, its highest level since 1986 while the gap with China increased 16.9 percent to $39.52 billion.

The balance-of-payments basis for recording U.S. trade via receipts from and payments to other countries includes adjustments for military shipments, nonmonetary gold, and inland freight trade with Canada and Mexico.
Census basis data uses information collected by the U.S. Customs Service on goods shipped across U.S. borders.
The department said that the non-petroleum trade deficit fell for the first time in four years, dropping to $107.79 billion last year from $111.72 billion in 1995.

The December deficit with the United Kingdom of $456 million was the highest since July 1987, the department said. The United States imported a record $2.8 billion worth of goods from the United Kingdom in December, primarily crude oil and related products.
